about: Savings levers: legitimate ways to cut a household's costs and tax, each with who it fits, what it saves, the real-world steps, a ready template and where to verify it. Content is paraphrased from official and public sources (cited by link, never copied), verified on the date shown and re-checked by its review date; a lever past its review date is shown as 'check before you act'. Not tax or legal advice: amounts and rules change every year. India first ('where'); a Global edition hides what does not apply.

levers.title: Rooftop solar with the central subsidy
levers.saves: Most of the electricity bill for 25 years, after a central subsidy of Rs 30,000 per kW for the first 2 kW and Rs 18,000 for the third (capped at Rs 78,000). Some states add their own.
steps: Find your consumer number and sanctioned load on the electricity bill.
Size it: about 1 kW for every 120 units a month you use.
Register on the national portal (pmsuryaghar.gov.in) with the consumer number and apply.
Pick a vendor registered on the portal; get two quotes in writing.
Your electricity company checks feasibility; then install.
Ask for the net meter and the inspection.
Upload the commissioning report and a cancelled cheque; the subsidy comes to your bank (DBT).

template.title: Quote request to a registered vendor
template.text: Hello, I have applied under PM Surya Ghar (consumer no. [number]). My average use is [units] units a month and my roof is about [sq ft] sq ft, [shade-free / partly shaded]. Please quote for a [size] kW grid-tied system with net metering: panel and inverter make and warranty, total price, what the subsidy covers, timeline and the after-sales contact. Thank you.

levers.confidence: official portal; amounts from public reports

levers.title: Solar on the society roof for common areas
levers.saves: Lower common-area electricity and so lower maintenance; the subsidy for housing societies is Rs 18,000 per kW for common facilities (including EV charging), up to 500 kW.
steps: Get last year's common-area electricity bills from the society office.
Raise it at the next managing committee meeting with the template below.
Apply through the national portal as a group housing society.
Follow the same vendor, net meter and DBT steps.

template.title: Note to the managing committee
template.text: Dear committee, our common-area electricity cost was about Rs [amount] last year. Under PM Surya Ghar, societies get Rs 18,000 per kW for common facilities. A [size] kW system could cut most of that bill and our maintenance. I propose we get two quotes from portal-registered vendors and decide at the next meeting. I am happy to coordinate.

levers.confidence: official portal; amounts from public reports

levers.title: Half fare for women on state buses
levers.saves: 50% of the fare on Maharashtra state transport (MSRTC) buses for every woman in the household.
steps: Each woman carries Aadhaar when she travels.
Get the transport mobility (NCMC) card where it is now asked for at the counter or depot: reports say it is required for concessions.
Use MSRTC for regular intercity trips instead of private buses or cabs.
levers.confidence: public reports; the card rule is recent: check at the depot

levers.title: Bus concessions for parents over 65
levers.saves: Reports describe 50% off MSRTC fares from about 65 and free travel after 75; the exact age bands differ between reports.
steps: Confirm the current age bands at the depot or on the MSRTC site.
Carry Aadhaar as age proof; get the mobility (NCMC) card if asked.
Book their regular trips on MSRTC.
levers.confidence: age bands differ between reports: confirm before relying on it

levers.title: Ayushman health cover for parents aged 70 and over
levers.saves: Hospital cover of up to Rs 5 lakh a year for every person aged 70 or more, whatever the family's income, under Ayushman Bharat (the Vay Vandana card). It can avoid or top up a costly senior health policy.
steps: Check the parent's age in Aadhaar (the scheme reads it from there).
Install the Ayushman app or open beneficiary.nha.gov.in; or visit a Common Service Centre.
Do the Aadhaar e-KYC with the mobile number linked to Aadhaar.
Download the card and keep it with their health papers.
If they already have CGHS or ECHS, compare and choose one: the rules let you keep only one.
levers.confidence: government scheme; cover amount from public reports

levers.title: Pick the cheaper tax regime, every year
levers.saves: The new regime is the default and, by public reports, gives a rebate that makes total income up to Rs 12 lakh tax-free, with a Rs 75,000 standard deduction for salaried people. The old regime can still win with large deductions (home-loan interest, 80C, 80D, HRA). The wrong choice can cost tens of thousands a year.
steps: Once a year, before declaring to your employer (or before advance tax), run the comparison on this card.
Tell your employer (salaried) or your tax filer which regime you choose.
Keep the proofs for any deduction you claim in the old regime.
levers.confidence: the Income-tax Act 2025 applies from 1 April 2026: confirm the figures on incometax.gov.in each year

levers.title: Ask your employer to pay part of your salary into NPS
levers.saves: An employer's NPS contribution (up to 14% of basic plus DA) is not taxed in the new regime, so the same cost to the employer leaves you more after tax, and it compounds for retirement.
steps: Ask HR whether the company offers employer NPS (corporate NPS) and at what share of basic.
Send the request below before the next salary cycle.
Check the next payslip shows the employer NPS line.

template.title: Request to HR
template.text: Dear HR, I would like part of my cost-to-company paid as an employer contribution to NPS (corporate model), up to the share of basic the policy allows. Please let me know the form and from which month it can start. Thank you.

levers.confidence: confirm the share and the section number under the 2025 Act

levers.title: Consultant or professional: presumptive tax
levers.saves: A professional or consultant with receipts up to Rs 75 lakh (when no more than 5% is in cash; else Rs 50 lakh) may declare 50% of receipts as income and keep no books. For the same gross, this is often far less tax than a salary, but there is no employer PF, gratuity or group cover, so budget for those yourself.
steps: Take fees by bank transfer, not cash, to stay inside the higher limit.
Fees usually arrive after 10% TDS: check it in your AIS/26AS each quarter.
Under the presumptive scheme, pay advance tax in one go by 15 March.
If receipts cross the GST threshold for services (Rs 20 lakh in most states), register for GST.
Buy your own health and term cover, and set up your own retirement saving (NPS or PPF), since no employer does it now.

template.title: Before you sign a consultancy contract
template.text: Fee per month and how it is paid (bank only) | TDS rate and when the certificate is issued | GST: who pays it, and is the client exempt | Notice period both ways | Leave and travel rules | What happens to the fee if the project stops | Your own health and term cover in place before day one

levers.confidence: section 58 of the 2025 Act per public commentary: confirm with a chartered accountant

levers.title: A Hindu Undivided Family (HUF), only when it fits
levers.saves: An HUF is a separate taxpayer with its own PAN and its own basic exemption, so income from ancestral property, or from gifts by relatives outside the HUF, can be taxed there instead of on your slab.
steps: Check the fit first: it helps only with ancestral property or gifts from relatives who are not members; your own salary or fees cannot be moved into it.
Draft the HUF deed (Karta and members), get its PAN, open its own bank account.
Keep its money strictly separate: a member's own money put in without consideration is taxed back on that member (clubbing).
File its own return every year, signed by the Karta.
Know the exit cost: dividing an HUF later takes a formal partition.
levers.confidence: sources differ on whether the rebate applies to an HUF: confirm with a chartered accountant before forming one

levers.title: Cut the recurring leaks
levers.saves: Subscriptions, add-on insurance on cards, unused memberships and auto-renewals: typically a few thousand rupees a month in most households, found from your own bank messages.
steps: Paste last month's bank and card messages in Money (the app finds every repeat payment).
For each one, keep, downgrade or cancel: decide once.
Cancel in the app or on the site that charges it, then delete the saved card there.
Next month, the app checks that the charge stopped.

levers.title: A safe, regular income for parents over 60
levers.saves: The Senior Citizens' Savings Scheme at a post office or bank pays a government-backed rate every quarter, usually above a fixed deposit; the rate is reset each quarter.
steps: Check this quarter's rate on India Post or your bank's site.
Open it at the post office or bank with the parent's KYC.
Choose quarterly payout into their savings account.
Diary the maturity date (the app adds it to your calendar).
levers.confidence: rate changes every quarter: check before opening
